answer: Each AI agent stakes a bonded token and registers a unique cryptographic identity anchored to a hardware-rooted prism. The network requires proof-of-work on a per-identity basis, forcing any new inlet to burn energy proportional to the stake. A malicious operator launching a Sybil swarm must acquire and lock capital equal to the total bonded value across all forged nodes, plus the continuous jetty cost of maintaining valid work, making large-scale attacks economically infeasible.
